title: Size every file by asking it for its metadata, not from the folder listing
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: A file created and grown by another process while held open (to >=256 MiB), listed at 0 B, is charged at its handle-reported size while the listing still shows 0 B: missing
A file held open with share mode 0 (no sharing) is still sized correctly because the metadata query asks for no data access: partial

After a scan, no file/folder in the temp tree has a changed creation/last-write/last-access/change timestamp, size, or attribute, verified independently, with fsutil disablelastaccess recorded: missing
On the temp tree, each folder's size equals the current on-disk bytes below it (held-open files and the hardlinked file included), checked against an independently computed expected total: partial
held-open-observers-dont-disturb: Parent LastAccessTime differs 6/6 around probes; isolated test: listing causes it, not probe (0/3)
probe-all-as-built-route-drive-time: Warm listing+as-built-probe-all took 188.3s (100.7 list + 87.6 probe) vs 150s cap; single-threaded listing alone ate 100.7s

Should a validate-stage drive-time regression (against the spike's self-imposed 150s warm / 10s-per-probe bars) block this slice, given none of the 7 person-agreed done-when criteria name a time budget and U-012 already marked the related compound bar impossible at the epic level? The design treats it as advisory; a person may disagree.

Is it acceptable that criterion 6's no-side-effects guarantee only holds for folders where the enumerating user's ACL grants FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, with a silent fallback to today's plain (atime-disturbing) open elsewhere -- or should such a folder be surfaced in the scan result rather than passed over quietly?

Whether to keep a cheap listing-based fast-skip for files whose listing has been stable across two directory refreshes (to cut probe volume) versus probing every eligible file unconditionally as this design does -- a perf/complexity tradeoff the data doesn't settle.

Whether the WOF-suspect-named ACE-denial test (AFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsAllocatedIsProbedOnlyWhenItIsWof) should be renamed now, since its name implies a gating condition that no longer exists, or left for whichever slice next touches OnDiskSizeTests.cs.
The overlapped bounded ProbePipeline (Submit/Drain/Complete, capacity 8192, concurrent with the listing): replaced by list-then-probe per accepted M-add-1.
The inline repeat-FileId probe that the design kept as a fallback lever: removed per accepted M4.

The M6 option of running the atime spike through the opt-in CfProvider sync root: not built or run, because it registers a real cldflt sync root on this PC, which SL-049 left for a person. OneDrive roots and cloud-marked folders are excluded instead.

The drive-time re-measurement on C: and the loopback-SMB probe-cost measurement: these are validate's work per the design and M-add-2. The counters they need (ListingTime, SizingTime, LongestProbe, LastAccessAsked/Kept) are built.
Recording Get-MpPreference EnableControlledFolderAccess: assigned to validate by the m7 decision. I did not read Defender settings.
Surfacing folders that refuse write-attributes in the scan result (the design's open question): not built. Only the internal LastAccessAsked/LastAccessKept counters exist, pending a person's answer.

Recognise sync roots from any cloud-files engine (Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud), not only OneDrive via the environment, or get a person's go-ahead to run the opt-in CfProvider check (placeholder in-sync state unchanged, no provider callbacks) before keeping last-access inside sync roots.

Validate: run a whole-drive C:\ scan with the built scanner and report ListingTime, SizingTime, LongestProbe and LastAccessAsked vs LastAccessKept against the spike's 188.3 s sequential baseline. I did not run it unattended because it issues the keep-last-access SetFileInformationByHandle call (measured as a no-op) on the person's own profile folders.
Validate: with a person's go-ahead, repeat the re-measurement through the SMB loopback rig and report per-probe latency beside listing time (M-add-2).
Add a settled rule fencing tests/HoldRig from FsAnalyser.Core (no ProjectReference, no FsAnalyser.Core name), as CfProvider has, so the observer stays independent of the code it checks.

The window's last progress tick can show pre-correction totals: C:\Program Files ended with CountersText at 32.0 GB on disk against the outcome's 32.1 GB, because the final batch lands after the last 250 ms tick. The pattern predates this slice, but sizing at the end makes it likelier; showing the final totals in CountersText at the ending would remove it.

A person answers the design's open question: should folders that refuse write-attributes (the majority on C:\Windows and Program Files) be surfaced in the scan result, rather than only counted internally?

attempts.summary: SL-056 replaced the scanner's listing-driven size-probe heuristic with an unconditional rule: probe every first-seen, non-link, non-cloud-only file through a metadata-only handle, apply results only on the listing thread, and suspend a folder's last-access time while listing it.
